text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by naming your endpoints simply, using nouns like /users or /orders instead of verbs. Each endpoint should do one job well. Always return the right HTTP status codes, such as 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API without guessing. Finally, plan for versioning from the beginning, for example /v1/users, so you can update your API later without breaking existing applications. Following these practices makes your API easier to use and maintain over time.
